title: Two-stage size caps (Content-Length header + actual bytes): Content-Length can lie
description: fetch_session, call, upload_blob, and download_blob all check Content-Length against the limit first (early exit before allocating), then re-check bytes.len() after the actual read. A contributor might argue the header check is redundant once the byte check exists, or that the byte check is redundant once the header is trusted. Neither simplification is correct: (1) Content-Length can be absent, wrong, or spoofed by a MITM — relying on it alone allows OOM; (2) checking only after reading defeats the early-exit purpose and allocates the full response before rejecting it. Both checks serve different purposes and must coexist.
